verdict: (1) Rod vs anchor, in the wood (convention A — the scale of the rod's alloy; one green-xylem α reading, 7.9 ppm/K; lib's titanium α values cite no source): on that one reading a titanium-alloy rod's term stays at or under 0.09 µm/K over the install-day axis 0–100 mm, and it does not cross the frames' 0.3 µm/K as long as α_w lies within 5.8–11.4 ppm/K (the alloys' windows intersected at 100 mm); tantalum, the opposite sign, reaches 0.14 µm/K there. The anchor (114) reaches ×2.6–×6.6 the frames at its deepest named tie, the PEEK sleeve carrying 90–99 % of it. (2) Above the bark the rod between the live bark and its clamp faces the scale, (α_s − α_rod)·h_c: with the in-wood term of a chosen 30 mm tie, a titanium rod stays under the frames for any scale within 7.8–20.2 ppm/K of the rod at install heights (h_c 13.5–35 mm, the ridge bark the clamp clears over DBH 38–60) and within 2.0 ppm/K at 135 mm (a fixed clamp set to clear twenty years of fast growth — a choice); a stainless-302 scale on a titanium rod costs 0.114–0.311 µm/K above the bark at install heights and up to 1.199 at 135 mm — for a steel or stainless scale this term dominates; a scale, probe and frame of the rod's own alloy cost nothing, isothermally. (3) A stainless rod is not supported: under convention A it reaches the frames near 32 mm (its α_w window at 30 mm, 7.28–27.28 ppm/K, ends just under the one reading); under convention B (the scale matched to the wood, the clamp at the dead bark's surface) near 18 mm on the thinnest bark (DBH 38) and over the frames at any tie on the thickest (DBH 60); mild steel under A near 72 mm. (4) Over the life the tie deepens at 0.8–5 mm/yr: under convention A, or with a clamp that keeps its height, the drift is |α_w − α_rod|·rate (titanium at most 0.0045 µm/K per year); with a fixed clamp it is |α_w − α_s|·rate — zero for a wood-matched scale. (5) For comparison with 114 on its datum and convention (B, 114's dead bark under the flange): stainless crosses near 24 / 11 mm below the live bark, the anchor at -0.7 / -13.3 mm (premise a — inside the dead bark) and 12.7 / ≈ 0 mm (premise b). (6) Not computed: the hole's grip on the rod, so no rod-vs-anchor bearing comparison; a non-uniform ΔT; frozen days (114's unfrozen share 0.72, an air criterion); whether the frames' 0.3 µm/K includes their own in-wood rod loop (commercial frames sit on rods); and the instrument's other terms — 0.3 µm/K is its whole budget.
